size.note: Collins Bird Guide gives 29–32 cm. Newman's Birds gives 30–31 cm.

habitat: Open woodland, bushveld, and grassland with perches, including the eastern lowveld. It avoids open arid country.
summary: A Palearctic migrant that spends the non-breeding season in Kruger. Most birds are present from December to March, with arrivals from October and occasional birds into May. Adults are pale blue or greenish on the head and underparts, with a brown back, blue wings tipped blue-black, and no tail streamers. The sexes look alike. The juvenile is a drabber version of the adult; part-by-part juvenile colours are not published in the sources used here, and the chick is not described.

similar.note: Lilac-breasted Roller has a lilac breast and long straight tail streamers. European Roller has neither.
Racket-tailed Roller has spatulate tips on the outer tail feathers. European Roller has no tail streamers.
Purple Roller has a white eyebrow and purple underparts streaked white, on a square tail.
Broad-billed Roller has a broad yellow bill and cinnamon upperparts.

viewNotes.note: Brown back and electric-blue wings, with blue-black ends to the flight feathers. There are no tail streamers.
Pale blue underparts and blue flight feathers ending blue-black. The texts used here do not give the underwing a separate colour from the upperwing.
Pale blue or greenish head and underparts face the viewer, without a lilac breast.
Brown upperparts and a tail without streamers.
Pale blue or greenish head and underparts, a brown back, and no tail streamers.

calls.description: Mostly silent in southern Africa, sometimes a harsh 'rack-kack, kacker'; the sexes are described as similar and are not given different calls.
A harsh, crow-like call, given as a raucous series when alarmed.
